text:
👁️ Думки. Колумністка The Atlantic Енн Епплбаум:

"Дії Трампа виглядають як спроба змусити Київ капітулювати. За останні кілька днів Трамп відкинув будь-які умовності, перекреслив десятиліття американської політики та звів нанівець 18 місяців власної дипломатії".

Епплбаум пише, що Трамп, скасувавши санкції проти РФ, порушив "як букву, так і дух законів, які сам же і підписав".

"Він погрожував припинити обмін розвідданими з Україною, якщо та не погодиться не завдавати ударів по російських НПЗ, — вимагаючи таким чином, щоб Київ відмовився від своєї найефективнішої зброї, і не вимагаючи нічого натомість від Росії", - зауважує вона.

Трамп також не засудив російські атаки на українські електростанції чи заводи — навіть ті, що належать американським компаніям.

"Він навіть не висловив співчуття у зв’язку із загибеллю українських дітей під час нещодавніх російських бомбардувань", - констатує Епплбаум.

"Президент натякав, що мета його нової політики — знизити ціни на пальне для американців. Можливо, він хоче переконати виборців, що причиною високих цін є Україна, а не його війна проти Ірану, яку він сам ініціював, — продовжує Епплбаум. — Але це не є достатнім поясненням чи виправданням. Обсяг пального, який Росія могла б експортувати, надто малий, вплив на ціноутворення — незначний, а сама теза з’явилася надто пізно, щоб вплинути на результати виборів", — стверджує вона.

"Натомість це виглядає зовсім інакше: як різка, відчайдушна спроба змусити Україну капітулювати та врятувати російську економіку — можливо, задля того, щоб нарешті укласти численні бізнес-угоди, які, як відомо, росіяни обговорювали з американськими переговірниками та іншими особами з оточення Трампа", — пише Епплбаум.

text: For at least three years Bellingcat has been covering Russia’s grain smuggling operation - shipping grain from occupied Ukraine . You can read our reporting on this here: https://www.bellingcat.com/?s=grain

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The recent escalation of Russian and Ukrainian attacks on Black Sea ports and commercial vessels threatens to further disrupt grain exports from two of the world’s largest suppliers, contributing to a sharp increase in global grain prices. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/31/war-and-heat-why-are-wheat-prices-soaring

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: Olof Gill, EU Commission spokesperson for Trade & Economic Security has called on EU member states Hungary, Poland and Slovakia to remove their bans on certain Ukrainian agricultural products, but so far no change has occurred.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: A third option - exporting grain via inland ports on the Danube River remains open. Far less grain can leave the country via this route and delays have occurred amid a shortage of personnel and critically low water levels. Satellite imagery shows a buildup of ships waiting near Danube river ports.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text:
India has exported more than 320 million unapproved synthetic opioid pills to West Africa in just three years. Trade data shows over 1,400 shipments of tapentadol — a potent painkiller — were sent to a region already facing an opioid crisis. Our investigation, with Indian publishing partner Newslaundry, found that more than 50% of the painkillers were high-strength (200mg+), doses not even approved for use in India.
Katherine de Tolly reports: https://www.bellingcat.com/news/2026/04/17/painkiller-pipeline-300-million-tapentadol-pills-sent-from-india-to-west-africa/?utm_source=mastodon

text:
After a funding warning appeared on NASA’s FIRMS site, many worried wildfire data access could be disrupted.
Fortunately, FIRMS continues to update daily — remaining an essential open-source resource for fire monitoring worldwide. https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/map/

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: NASA FIRMS was a good starting point, helping our researchers confirm when the fires were first detected. NASA FIRMS uses a colour classification system to show how long ago an active fire was detected. A yellow square indicated this latest wildfire was first detected at 15:25 on Sept, 22.

yes, that's possible!
the way we do it is a getting the SSL certificates, calculate hashes for archived media and the certificates, and then timestamp those with external services.
We have two timestamping alternatives: one is blockchain based https://auto-archiver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/autogen/enricher/opentimestamps_enricher.html
The other relies on RFC3161 timestamping authorities https://auto-archiver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/autogen/enricher/timestamping_enricher.html - both are free.
Here's an example from a recent tweet where both timestamping strategies are used: https://bellingcat-archive.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/no-dups/60b4da5262174b5c403abced/bdc9da4201174fa1ae19f27f.html

text: During the Arab Spring, social media became a powerful tool for sharing real-time evidence through photos, videos, and testimonies. author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: These methods could also be useful for other elections and political events, as ad spending data from tech platforms can provide researchers and journalists with insights into trends that often align with a campaign’s offline strategies.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: This analysis reveals some key strategic differences of both campaigns: none of the Trump team’s top word pairs referred to specific issues or policies – instead including many strong action-based phrases such as “request ballot” and “get tickets”.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: Meanwhile, aside from “President Trump” some of the most common keyword pairs in Republican campaign’s ads were “AMERICA GREAT” and “GREAT AGAIN”. This was used in the context of “Make America Great Again”, the slogan popularised by Trump during his 2016 campaign.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The pair of words that appeared most frequently in the Democratic campaign’s ads was “Donald Trump”, with their own nominee’s name following in second place. Harris’ campaign also often mentioned Project 2025 to attack Trump who has been trying to distance himself from the initiative.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: To get a rough idea of the key themes in each campaign’s ads on Facebook and Instagram, we used a Python tool that helps break down text into unique word combinations and count them.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The seven swing states – Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin – are regarded as holding key positions in the 2024 election. The Democrats have outspent Republicans in each of those states.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: Both figures likely represent just the tip of the iceberg for the candidates’ total ad spending across television and digital advertising including on other online platforms such as Google.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: Almost all (99.8 percent) of the ads sponsored by Harris’ campaign ran on both Facebook and Instagram, whereas almost 26 percent of those supporting Trump were only shown on Facebook, and 7.5 percent targeted only Instagram.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: By summing up the average spending for all ads by each candidate’s campaigns, we found that Harris’ campaign has spent about US$113 million – advertising on Facebook and Instagram between July 21 and Oct. 30, while Trump’s campaign spent about US$17 million.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The data from Meta’s Ad Library does not show a specific amount of spending for each ad, but rather gives a range with an “upper limit” and “lower limit” reflecting the maximum and minimum amounts spent on the ad respectively.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: You can process the data with Python to see the regions that were targeted most by each campaign, or look at the demographic information, showing what percentage of an ad was aimed at a specific gender within different age groups.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The files downloaded from the Meta Ad Library includes details on the ads such as the pages and platforms they appeared on, the dates they were created, which states they targeted, a range for the amount spent and the text and links that appeared with each ad.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: In total, we found 17 different advertisers with ads sponsored by Harris’ campaign, and six with ads sponsored by Trump’s official campaign.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: Bellingcat downloaded all ads published by pages that share an ad sponsor with the official pages of Harris and Trump. We then removed ads with sponsors not listed on the candidates’ pages, to limit the results to accounts associated with the candidates’ official campaigns.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: A more reliable way to identify ads sponsored by the candidates’ official sponsors is to go to the “About” section on their official accounts, which provides information about all the sponsors associated with that page, as well as other pages that share those sponsors.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: CNN reported last month, for instance, that the Harris campaign had spent US$11 million on an obscure page called “The Daily Scroll”. https://edition.cnn.com/2024/10/15/politics/daily-scroll-facebook-harris-campaign-ads/index.html

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: When looking at data for the Democratic and Republican candidates, Harris and Trump’s official accounts respectively were an obvious starting point. However, their campaigns’ spending was not limited to ads running from their official pages.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: When looking for an advertiser and the country the ads are targeting, results display all ads that are currently active. But you can tweak the filters to also include ads that ran during the specified time period but are no longer active.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: The Meta Ad Library is a resource that provides details of ad spending across Meta’s platforms – including Facebook, Instagram, the Meta Audience Network and Messenger – in a specific time period.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: We found that ahead of the 2024 US presidential election on Nov. 5, Democratic candidate Kamala Harris’ campaign mentioned the phrase “Donald Trump” more than they did “Kamala Harris” in ads on Facebook and Instagram.

author: @Bellingcat@mstdn.social
text: We break down how we analysed the campaigns of Donald Trump and Kamala Harris and got insights into which states they targeted, their estimated ad spending and some of the key themes that appeared in the ads.
